stem:
Ojas splits a chickpea seed and counts two cotyledons. The young plant later shows reticulate (netted) leaf veins and a taproot. A maize seed he opens has one cotyledon. In class he learns that two cotyledons mark a dicotyledon and one marks a monocotyledon, and that dicotyledons have reticulate venation with a taproot while monocotyledons have parallel venation with a fibrous root system.

Which claim correctly connects the chickpea?

options.text: The chickpea is a dicotyledon with reticulate venation and a taproot system.
The chickpea is a dicotyledon with parallel venation and a taproot system.
The maize is a dicotyledon with reticulate venation and a taproot system.
The chickpea is a monocotyledon with parallel venation and a fibrous root system.

teacher.key_rationale: Two cotyledons mark a dicotyledon, which has reticulate venation and a taproot. Parallel venation with a taproot mixes terms; calling maize a dicotyledon omits its one-cotyledon condition; calling the chickpea a monocotyledon with parallel veins and a fibrous root reverses the link.
